title: Agreement of valid position tags
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $y$ be a Boolean input word, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $y$. If $b$ is a Boolean tag that is false at the left boundary and true at the right boundary, then the displacement vector computed using $b$ equals the vector computed using the tag that is true exactly when the input-head position is nonzero.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$b$ correctly tags the two boundary positions
replaced: Let $c$ be a source configuration and let $b$ be any valid position tag for its input position. The displacement vector computed from $b$ equals the displacement vector computed from the deterministic nonzero-position tag; at an interior cell either tag yields the same clamped movement.
